title: Composition for the dualizing complex
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let
$d:F\to X$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism with $a_X$ and $a_F=a_X\circ d$
exceptionally admissible. Then there is a
canonical isomorphism

$$
Rd^!\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\omega_{F,A},
$$

functorial in $d$, where $\omega_{X,A}$, $\omega_{F,A}$ are the
dualizing complexes of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] and $Rd^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image of
$d$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $L_f=Rf_!$ and $R_f=Rf^!$. By [def-trf-admissibility], the three morphisms $d,a_X,a_F$ have specified adjunctions $L_f\dashv R_f$ on these categories. The hypotheses give admissibility for the two structure morphisms; for $d$ the same definition explicitly states that every separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes is admissible. Thus all three adjunctions have the same finite coefficient ring $A$ and the same constructible finite-Tor domains. Clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] supplies the natural isomorphism $\alpha:L_{a_X}L_d\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{a_F}$, with its identity and associativity equations. Only this compact-support composition clause is used from that package.

Apply [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] to $L_d$ and $L_{a_X}$: $R_dR_{a_X}$ is right adjoint to $L_{a_X}L_d$, with pasted counit. The same left functor has right adjoint $R_{a_F}$: explicitly transport $L_{a_F}\dashv R_{a_F}$ along $\alpha$ by the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(L_{a_X}L_dK,N)\xrightarrow{h\mapsto h\alpha_K^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}(L_{a_F}K,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,R_{a_F}N)$. The canonical right-adjoint comparison in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] therefore gives a natural isomorphism $\chi_{d,a_X}:R_dR_{a_X}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{a_F}$. More explicitly, $\chi_{d,a_X,N}$ is the $L_{a_F}\dashv R_{a_F}$ transpose of
$$L_{a_F}R_dR_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}}L_{a_X}L_dR_dR_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{L_{a_X}\varepsilon_d}L_{a_X}R_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{a_X}}N.$$
This specifies the comparison rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the objects; the inverse is the reverse right-adjoint comparison. The displayed formula uses precisely the pasted counit asserted by the cited node.

The constant complex $A_s$ is in $\mathcal D_s$: its sole cohomology sheaf is the constant finite rank-one free $A$-module, hence constructible. For every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules in degree zero, the free rank-one complex $A_s$ itself is a flat model and $A_s\otimes_A^L M=M$, so cohomology outside degree zero vanishes. This gives Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with the finite coefficient ring of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Evaluate $\chi_{d,a_X}$ at $A_s$. By [def-trf-dualizing-complex], $R_{a_X}A_s=\omega_{X,A}$ and $R_{a_F}A_s=\omega_{F,A}$. The resulting component is the required canonical isomorphism $R_d\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{F,A}$.

source.place: Second paragraph: evaluate the composition isomorphism at the constant complex

proof.text:
Here is the compatibility with further composition. Let $e:H\to F$ be another separated finite-type morphism in the same setting and put $a_H=a_Xde$. Compare the two maps $R_eR_dR_{a_X}N\to R_{a_H}N$: first $R_e(\chi_{d,a_X,N})$ followed by $\chi_{e,a_F,N}$, or first $\theta_{e,d,R_{a_X}N}$ followed by $\chi_{de,a_X,N}$. Here, writing $\alpha_{d,e}:L_dL_e\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{de}$ for the compact-support comparison, define $\theta_{e,d,M}:R_eR_dM\to R_{de}M$ to be the $L_{de}\dashv R_{de}$ transpose of $\varepsilon_{d,M}\circ L_d(\varepsilon_{e,R_dM})\circ\alpha_{d,e,R_eR_dM}^{-1}$; it is an isomorphism by the same right-adjoint-composition statement used in Step 2. After the associativity identification $L_{a_H}\cong L_{a_X}L_dL_e$ of [prop-functor-package], their transposes are both
$$L_{a_X}L_dL_eR_eR_dR_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{L_{a_X}L_d\varepsilon_e}L_{a_X}L_dR_dR_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{L_{a_X}\varepsilon_d}L_{a_X}R_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{a_X}}N.$$
For the first path, naturality of $\varepsilon_e$ gives $\varepsilon_{e,R_{a_F}N}\circ L_eR_e(\chi_{d,a_X,N})=\chi_{d,a_X,N}\circ\varepsilon_{e,R_dR_{a_X}N}$; after moving $\chi_{d,a_X,N}$ past this counit, its defining transpose formula in Step 2 gives the last two displayed arrows. For the second path, the counit-compatibility and pasted-counit clause of [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition], applied first to $e,d$ at $R_{a_X}N$, replaces their combined counit by $L_d\varepsilon_e$ followed by $\varepsilon_d$; applying the $a_X$ counit gives exactly the same three arrows. In detail, the associativity equation is
$$\alpha_{a_F,e}\circ(\alpha_{a_X,d}L_e)=\alpha_{a_X,de}\circ(L_{a_X}\alpha_{d,e}).$$
Taking its inverse gives the same initial map from $L_{a_H}$ to $L_{a_X}L_dL_e$ in both transposes. The adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so the two component maps agree. For identities, let $\lambda_T:L_{\mathrm{id}_T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_T}$ be the compact-support unit isomorphism. The canonical isomorphism $u_T:R_{\mathrm{id}_T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_T}$ has components $u_{T,M}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}_T,M}\circ\lambda_{T,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M}^{-1}$: transport the specified identity-morphism adjunction along $\lambda_T$ and compare its right adjoint with that of $\mathrm{id}\dashv\mathrm{id}$ by [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] (take both functors to be identities). In particular $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}_T,M}=u_{T,M}\circ\lambda_{T,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M}$. For the source identity and $g:T\to U$, the unit equation $\alpha_{g,\mathrm{id}_T}=L_g\lambda_T$ makes the transpose of $\chi_{\mathrm{id}_T,g,M}$ equal to
$$\varepsilon_{g,M}\circ L_g(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}_T,R_gM}\circ\lambda_{T,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}R_gM}^{-1})
=\varepsilon_{g,M}\circ L_g(u_{T,R_gM}).$$
By the adjunction bijection this gives $\chi_{\mathrm{id}_T,g,M}=u_{T,R_gM}$. For the target identity and $f:V\to T$, use $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_T,f}=\lambda_TL_f$. Naturality of $\lambda_T$ makes the transpose of $\chi_{f,\mathrm{id}_T,M}$ equal to
$$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}_T,M}\circ\lambda_{T,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M}^{-1}\circ\varepsilon_{f,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M}
=u_{T,M}\circ\varepsilon_{f,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M}
=\varepsilon_{f,M}\circ L_fR_f(u_{T,M}),$$
where the final equality is counit naturality for $f$. Hence $\chi_{f,\mathrm{id}_T,M}=R_f(u_{T,M})$. Thus these comparisons are identities after the canonical identifications $R_{\mathrm{id}_T}\cong\mathrm{id}$, without requiring the specified functor or counit to be literally identities. Evaluating these equations at $N=A_s$ proves functoriality in $d$.
